The Encyclopædia Britannica calls Edel "the foremost 20th-century authority on the life and works of Henry James ." His work on James won him both a National Book Award and a Pulitzer Prize .

# Leon Edel

## Finalist , 1980 **National Book Awards**  
Finalist , 1981 **National Book Awards**  
Finalist , **National Book Awards 1973**  
Winner , **National Book Awards 1963**

Leon Edel was Henry James Professor of English and American Letters at New York University. He received both the 1963 Pulitzer Prize and the 1963 National Book Award for the second and third volumes of his seminal five-volume biography of the American novelist and critic Henry James. Edel also edited books on James’s letters, plays, essays, criticism, and stories, and wrote introductions to new editions of James’s novels. In addition to his writings about James, Mr. Edel was the editor of four volumes of Edmund Wilson’s papers, wrote biographies of Willa Cather, Henry David Thoreau, and  a book about the Bloomsbury circle.
